tagline: The westernmost tip of Africa — a surf-and-music capital on a peninsula, facing the slave-trade island of Gorée.
overview: Dakar is Africa's westernmost city — a peninsula capital that points into the Atlantic, where the 49-metre African Renaissance Monument (taller than the Statue of Liberty) watches over surf breaks and fishing beaches.

Twenty minutes offshore lies Gorée Island — the pastel colonial island that became a UNESCO memorial to the Atlantic slave trade, visited by Mandela and Obama. The city's own heart is the Marché Sandaga chaos and the mbalax music clubs that made Youssou N'Dour a global star.
Speed's 2025 Africa tour streamed from Dakar to Senegalese crowds — the country's teranga (hospitality) is famous across the continent.

funFacts.text: Cap-Vert peninsula is mainland Africa's westernmost point.

funFacts.title: AFRICAN RENAISSANCE
funFacts.text: The 49m bronze family monument — taller than the Statue of Liberty — crowns a volcanic hill.

funFacts.title: GORÉE ISLAND
funFacts.text: The House of Slaves' 'Door of No Return' is the Atlantic slave trade's most visited memorial.

funFacts.title: MBALAX
funFacts.text: Senegal's drum-driven music — Youssou N'Dour's genre — owns the city's nights.

funFacts.title: TERANGA
funFacts.text: 'Hospitality' is so central to Wolof identity it names the national character.

funFacts.title: THE PINK LAKE
funFacts.text: Lake Retba's salt-heavy water turns pink — an hour north.

funFacts.title: THE FISHING CITY
funFacts.text: Colourful pirogues still land fish on city beaches each evening.

funFacts.title: DAKAR RALLY
funFacts.text: The Paris-Dakar rally was named for its finish here — it moved to South America, then Saudi.

funFacts.title: SANDAGA
funFacts.text: The colonial-era market is one of West Africa's biggest.

funFacts.title: A CITY OF SUFI
funFacts.text: The Mouride and Tidjane brotherhoods shape the city's religious culture — Touba's grand mosque is a pilgrimage.
